The Yaroslavl Great Panagia Icon of the Theotokos

Icons

Theotokos

The Yaroslavl Great Panagia Icon of the Theotokos

Yaroslavl Oranta · Great Panagia · Mother of God of the Incarnation

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

The Yaroslavl Great Panagia is a monumental medieval icon now in the Tretyakov Gallery. Its museum title is Mother of God of the Incarnation, with Great Panagia in parentheses. It is distinct from the Yaroslavl Tenderness icon.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 9, 10, 16, 18, 19

What is depicted

Mary stands frontally with hands raised in prayer. Christ appears in a medallion before her and blesses with both hands; angels occupy the upper corners. The museum discusses the familiar term Orans while noting that scholarly names for this particular composition have varied.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 19, 20

History and tradition

The gallery dates the panel to the first quarter of the thirteenth century, perhaps around 1224. It was rediscovered at Yaroslavl’s Transfiguration monastery in 1919 and entered the gallery in 1930. The proposed connection with the monastery cathedral remains a probable attribution, not an established commission record.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 10, 17, 18

The catalogue identifies inventory 12796, a large wooden panel measuring 193.5 by 120 centimeters, painted in egg tempera.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 12, 13, 14, 16

Published explanation

The museum’s explanation centers on the Incarnation and its liturgical significance. It interprets Mary’s prayerful pose in relation to the intercession of the Church and discusses the Child’s episcopal gesture. These are attributed museum interpretations of this object; no unsupported color code or additional symbolism is supplied.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 19, 20, 21
